🗣️ Key Talking Points for Students

1
You don't need a university degree

Most aviation careers — pilot, AME, ATCO, avionics — are entered through college programs or direct licensing. University engineering is one path, not the only path.

2
The industry is desperate for people

Canada faces a critical shortage across all aviation roles. Graduating into this field means job offers before graduation in many programs.

3
Salaries are competitive — and growing

AMEs earn $65K–$120K. ATCOs $80K–$160K. Airline captains $180K–$250K+. These aren't entry-level figures — but progression is faster than in most fields.

4
STEM is a pathway, not a barrier

Strong math and physics open more doors, but many technical roles require trade-level academics, not academic excellence. Curiosity and hands-on aptitude matter more.

5
Aviation is more diverse than it looks

Careers span operations, logistics, IT, safety, management, manufacturing, and more. There's a role for every student — including those who don't want to fly.

❓ Common Student & Parent Objections

My marks aren't good enough
Most aviation programs admit on aptitude and passion, not just grades. College flight programs, AME programs, and RPAS certifications have accessible entry requirements. AACP's ACIA™ assessment helps students understand their fit.
Flight training is too expensive — we can't afford it
Training costs are real, but scholarships, bursaries, and airline sponsorship programs exist. Some carriers offer cadet programs that fund training in exchange for a service commitment. AACP can connect students with funding pathways.
Is aviation a stable career? What about layoffs?
The 2020 disruption was real, but the structural shortage that followed is lasting. Transport Canada projects demand will outpace supply through 2033+. Skilled aviation tradespeople remained employed even during the peak of COVID restrictions.
My daughter wants to be a pilot — but it's so male-dominated
The industry is actively working to change this. Organizations like IAWA Canada and WIA offer mentorship. Airlines are specifically recruiting women. The workforce is shifting and representation is growing — now is a great time to enter.

🏫 Bring Aviation to Your School

1
Connect a student to AACP

Refer any student showing interest to aviationaerospacecompetency.com — they can explore pathways and take the ACIA™ assessment.

2
Request a school visit or virtual session

AACP can arrange aviation professionals and educators to present to your class or career fair. No cost to schools.

3
Integrate into your programming

Add aviation pathway information to your Grade 10–12 career exploration resources. AACP materials are available in English and French.

4
Share this hub with your students

This page is publicly accessible. Send the link or QR code to any student who expresses interest in aviation or aerospace.

What We Offer

AACP Programs & Pathways

Aviation & Aerospace Competency Program supports students, schools, and educators across Canada.

Career Discovery

✦ ACIA™

The Aviation Career Intelligence Assessment (ACIA™) helps students discover which aviation and aerospace careers best match their strengths, interests, and learning profile — before they commit to a training path.

  • Psychometric career compatibility scoring
  • Personalized pathway report
  • Covers 40+ aviation and aerospace roles
  • Available to any student, free of charge
Refer a Student Learn More
Skills Training

🛸 RPAS Workforce Hub

AACP's RPAS Workforce Hub provides Transport Canada–aligned drone pilot certification training and workforce development for students entering the fastest-growing segment of Canadian aviation.

  • Basic and Advanced RPAS operations
  • Transport Canada Small RPAS certification pathway
  • Practical and written exam preparation
  • Industry employer connections and workforce placement
